synopsis: UN R171 covers on-road Driver Control Assistance Systems, including Level 2 assistance in cars, and does not apply to off-road machines [f1766, f2826, f8111]. Physical testing remains the default; virtual testing is permitted for hard-to-reproduce scenarios after a rigorous toolchain credibility evaluation, rather than as a simulation-only regime [f1769, f1217, f8110]. When virtual testing is used, an Annex 5 credibility assessment must be submitted to the Type Approval Authority, demonstrating tool scope, scenario validity and toolchain validation [f15406, f2488, f2489]. The corpus dates the regulatory text to 2024–2025 and the original series publication to 2025; a vendor attributes the addition of virtual testing to late 2024, while the 02 series was still under discussion in January 2026 [f7681, f2827, f1276, f2490]. For off-road validation, the booklet recommends borrowing R171-style credibility packages and qualifying simulation against physical tests, but reports no identified capability-building or validation-duration estimates for the R171 precedent [f2143, f2648, f1768].
